Tom — attaching the latest OrderForm (v3) that reflects the 12-month renewal and the requested 30% capacity uplift for the next term. Key points: 

- Renewal term: 12 months (starts on existing term expiry)
- Capacity: +30% across inference tokens and embeddings, with separate metering for Dedicated pools
- Billing: monthly in arrears; PRORATION: we set a full-month proration for mid-cycle changes (see section 4) — flagged for legal review

From: Samantha Ortiz <sam.ortiz@cranford.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cranford.com>
Cc: procurement@cranford.com
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: 12-month renewal + 30% capacity uplift (OrderForm v3)

Evelyn — thank you. Our legal team reviewed OrderForm-v3 and attached a redline (Redlines_OrderForm.docx) with comments. High-level items we need to discuss: 

1) Termination notice: want to increase notice to 60 days for non-renewal (was 30).
2) SLA credits: need clearer metric definition and what triggers credits for token-level latency breaches.
3) Billing proration: prefer prorated billing to be calculated at daily granularity rather than full-month when capacity changes mid-cycle. This impacts our internal chargeback.
4) Data retention & deletion: require a 30-day guaranteed delete window for ephemeral logs plus SOC 2 attestation on retention practices.

I’ve highlighted language in the redline and added rationale on each clause. Procurement is on copy for the billing/proration conversation. Please loop in Redwood legal if you need alternate wording.

Attachments: Redlines_OrderForm.docx

Regards,
Samantha Ortiz
Senior Counsel — Data & Contracts
Cranford Analytics
sam.ortiz@cranford.com

Samantha — thanks for the redline and the clear notes. I reviewed the flagged items and propose the following compromises (attached as Proposed_Compromise_v1.docx with inline edits):

- Termination notice: accept 60 days for non-renewal; propose a 45-day mutual notice for operational flexibility (we can match 60 if Cranford requires it as a hard term).
- SLA credits: define the SLA thresholds by percentile (p95 latency per route) and cap credits to a percentage of monthly spend; include an escalation path with performance remediation plan.
- Billing proration: we can support daily prorations but need to keep minimum invoice unit at 1 day to avoid microinvoices. Proposed language: \"Proration will be calculated on a per-day basis where any change effective mid-billing cycle will be charged or credited pro rata based on the number of days in the billing period.\"
- Data retention: Redwood will guarantee deletion of ephemeral request logs within 30 days and provide a SOC 2 evidence package upon request; add a customer-requested export window clause.

Two quick operational asks for procurement: 
- Please confirm whether Cranford needs invoices on the 1st of month or on renewal anniversary dates (this affects proration calculations).
- If Cranford requires daily proration rounding to cents, we will need to align finance systems; otherwise we will round to the nearest dollar per invoice.

If this compromise looks reasonable I’ll incorporate the edits into OrderForm-v3 and prepare a DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
